# Data

All code to reproduce the results of this thesis are released [here](https://github.com/bbtheo/ds-thesis).

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(scales)

prevalence <- read_csv(
  "data/external/dataset_fraud_prevalence.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    fraud_rate = n_fraud / n_rows,
    dataset_label = reorder(dataset_label, fraud_rate)
  )

prevalence_eu_cc

```

## Datasets

<!-- TODO: change all hard coded amount to the dataset prevalence data -->

- as the topic of fraud in banking is so sensitive a limited amount of datasets are freely available.
    - Used all datasets that i could find that have transaction level fraud tags and are freely useable
- in total 6 public transaction datasets
- eu_cc (ULB) 284 807 observations with 30 features 0.172% fraud prevalence (or 492 fraudulend transactions) it has been collected a industry participant and contains a subset of online transactions for two day period.[@dalpozzolo2015calibrating] 
- banksim 594 643 observations 7 feature 1.2% fraud prevalence (or 7200 fraudulend transactions). Data is generated by agent based simulation, this simulation was tuned on data provided by a spanish bank.
    - As it is simulator based and could be then produce as long of a sequence as possible. In this thesis we will use the original authors canonical own kaggle posting that can be found (here)[https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ealaxi/banksim1]. <!-- TODO: add a citation to the kaggle -->
    - Simulation is run 180 "steps" which represent approximately 6 months worth of observations.
-paysim another agent based simulation by @lopezrojas2016_paysim. Rather than using the full 23 million observation from the original paper, in this thesis i used a 1/4 scaled down version from [kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ealaxi/paysim1).<!-- TODO: add a citation to the kaggle --> In this downscaled dataset has 6 362 620 observations and 0.13% fraud prevalence.
- baf by @jesus2022baf_arxiv 1 million observations 1.1% fraud prevalence. This dataset is also synthetically produced, compared to other previous datasets this one represents so called application fraud. The predicted observations are not transactions rather they are   
- fifar from @alves2023fifar_learning_to_defer is a subset of observations from BAF. 600k observations 1.2% fraud prevalence. 
    - It is keot as it has some benchmarks and contain a canonical test-train split that makes model comparison easier
- Datasets that were ultimately dropped:
    - ai_banking 10k, 28.4% — dev-only, excluded (near-balanced, unsuitable as an imbalance benchmark) [@talha2025ai_powered_banking_fraud]
    - cc_2025 poorly constructed synthetic dataset where the fraud labels were randomly seeded [@rajak2025credit_card_fraud_2025]. The reasons why this was dropped from the study will be studied deeper in @sec-app-cc.
- Only eu_cc is real transaction data other datasets are simulations and synthetic constructions.
